Partnership for Community Development Help us transform Fayette St. Park! In 2025, the Village of Earlville received $627,847 through the Office of Parks, Recreation, and Historic Preservation for the redesign and construction of the pavilion, playground, and skate park on Fayette St. The PCD has been working with the Village and the Earlville community since 2020 to revitalize this important community space. With the planned construction of new senior housing in the adjacent former school building, Fayette St. Park will be transformed into a unique multi-generational space in southern Madison County. The PCD is excited to work with Earlville to make the community’s vision a reality. We are currently accepting donations to match the grant funding for this project. It is actively moving forward projects related to housing, parks, trails, street design, community centers and small business grants.
In addition, the PCD encompasses The Hamilton Chamber of Commerce and The Hub Small Business Incubator under its fiscal umbrella.
They also provide support with grants and networking events.
The Hub is the only state certified business incubator in Madison County and provides coworking, networking, mentoring, and business development programming for the entire county.
The PCD helped the Village of Hamilton obtain a $2.25 million New York Forward Grant that will include projects that impact the Village Green, new downtown development, and facade renovations.
A Transportation Alternatives Program grant through NYSDOT will bring another $1.8 million to the village in streetscape improvements and trail connections.
Supporting Businesses The Hub Business Incubator The Hub is managed by PCD and is CNY’s only state-certified business incubator.
The Hub offers business advising and mentorship, co-working, networking, and more.

History In August 1998, representatives from the Town of Hamilton, the Village of Hamilton, and Colgate University came together to discuss shared concerns and opportunities for collaboration. Their focus was on revitalizing the local economy and enhancing the quality of life for residents. Key issues identified during these discussions included small business development, downtown façade improvements, and the restoration of the Village Green. As a result, the Partnership for Community Development (PCD) was established in 1999 as a non-profit organization. Rooted in the spirit of collaboration, PCD brings together its founding partners—along with other local governments and community organizations—to facilitate cooperative projects that strengthen the community.
